title: Unify policy orchestration & stabilize fallback reconciliation in smart router
creator: Marco Lin
description:
Background: Over the last 18 months the smart router accumulated multiple overlapping policy evaluation paths (legacy policy-adapters and a newer policy compiler). This has led to two classes of issues: (1) non-deterministic fallback ordering when regional capacity degrades, and (2) contention hotspots from per-request locks in the policy evaluation hotpath. The goals of this ticket are to unify policy orchestration into a single deterministic pipeline, remove duplicate evaluation shims, and stabilize the fallback reconciliation so the fallback chain is reproducible and auditable across regions.

Scope: 1) Extract a single policy orchestration interface that normalizes inputs for route scoring (region, model variant, cost tier, latency SLO). 2) Replace the current ad-hoc fallback chain with a deterministic reconciler that produces stable, ordered fallback lists and exposes a tracing header for debugging. 3) Reduce runtime contention by replacing coarse global locks with fine-grained shard-based routing state and lock-free reads for cached prefix/KV decisions. 4) Upgrade rules-engine dependency from v1.7.2 -> v2.0.0 (breaking API changes require adapter). 5) Add unit/e2e tests and a canary rollout plan.

Non-goals: We are not changing routing policy semantics (policy language) in this ticket, only the orchestration and execution path. No user-facing API changes are planned for this release.
acceptance_criteria: Unified policy orchestration compiles the same policy graph for existing unit test suite with no semantic drift
Fallback reconciler returns deterministic ordered fallbacks for a given request fingerprint across repeated runs
End-to-end median tail latency for routing decision hotpath decreases by >= 15% under our synthetic test harness
Rules-engine dependency upgraded to v2.0.0 with adapter shim removed in runtime-1.22 branch
Canary rollout shows no increase in error rates or fallback invocations for 48h at 1% traffic
Documentation updated and a tracing header (X-RW-Routing-Trace) is emitted for all fallback decisions
migration_plan: Add adapters that translate old policy-adapter outputs to new orchestration input format (short-lived)
Run synthetic load tests in staging with region failure injection to validate deterministic fallback ordering
Merge to runtime-1.22 branch behind feature flag 'routing.unified_orchestration'
Canary rollout at 1% traffic for 48h, observe metrics (errors, avg fallback length, decision latency)
Progressively increase canary to 10%, 50% following successful checks and remove feature flag after 2 weeks
rollout_plan: Week 0: internal rollout to dev/staging; run benchmark suite and chaos scenarios
Week 1: Canary 1% for 48h, regressions triaged by oncall and owners
Week 2: Canary 10% for 72h if no regressions; collect cost/latency deltas
Week 3: Canary 50% for 72h and run full query sweep
Week 4: Gradual global rollout and feature flag removal if stable
notes: Trade-offs: We preserve policy syntax to avoid PRs across policy authors, but adapter code increases short-term complexity.
Performance: Shard-based routing state reduces lock contention but increases memory footprint slightly (estimated +4%).
Compatibility: Rules-engine v2 exposes a new score normalization step; we mirror v1 semantics in the adapter tests before flipping the switch.
Telemetry: New metrics added: routing.decision_latency_ms, routing.fallback_chain_length, routing.reconciler_runs_total
Fallback UX: The reconciler will tag fallback items with 'reason' enum to aid runtime analysis and console visibility.
comments: 2025-06-03 — Marco Lin: Initial spike completed. Identified two hotspots: global_policy_lock and legacy-adapter translation. Prototype shows ~22% improvement in decision throughput when replacing the lock with per-shard RW guards.
2025-06-10 — Aisha Patel: Raised concern about rules-engine v2 hash change affecting A/B experiments. Decided to implement adapter normalization layer to keep experiment tags stable during migration.

2025-06-18 — Priya Nair (SRE): Ran failure injection in staging (simulated region outage in eu-west). Observed inconsistent fallback order across runs on main; reconciler prototype produced stable ordering. Created dashboard panel for fallback_chain_length.
2025-06-25 — Design review (internal): PM asked for a tracing header and explicit 'reason' codes in the reconciler for Console visibility. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-07-05 — Code review: ENG reviewers requested clearer separation between orchestration and policy evaluation. Split the PR into two: orchestration core + adapter (PR 4822) and fallback reconciler (PR 4824).

2025-07-12 — Load test: Synthetic harness at 5k rps reduced median decision latency from 12.4ms -> 9.8ms and tail (p99) from 48ms -> 39ms. Memory usage up ~3.7% on serving nodes. Marked as promising but continued monitoring needed.
2025-07-16 — Security: Security team validated that no new sensitive data leaves the control plane; recommended adding unit test to assert no policy secrets are serialized in the trace header.
2025-07-18 — Aisha Patel: Merged orchestration core behind feature flag. Starting canary next week at 1%. Added follow-up ticket to remove adapter after 6 weeks if stable: ENG-22012.
